data.narrative:
Pivot Bio, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $920.9M to date, is evaluated against a comparable universe of nine private firms and one public company in the sector. The peer set includes stage-adjacent businesses such as Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), Bedrock Robotics (Series B, $1.8B), and Dexterity (Series B, $1.6B), alongside established players like Agile Robots and Nimble Robotics.

Two valuation methods converge on a consistent range. The stage-progression method, applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage step-ups to the $921M capital raised proxy, implies a valuation of $1.6B. The peer-median approach across seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields an identical $1.6B median, with a distribution spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. Both methods are applicable given the availability of recent private financings and a defined peer cohort.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $1.6B. Key uncertainties include stage-relative positioning within the peer cohort—the presence of both Series B and Series D comparables introduces variance—and the representativeness of recent private-market multiples in a sector where deployment cycles and customer concentration remain material drivers of risk.
